approachQuestion.prompt:
Remove Ends to Reach a Total

An array `tokens` holds non-negative amounts. In one operation remove either the first or last remaining token. Return the fewest operations whose removed values sum to exactly target, or -1 if impossible. Removing no tokens is allowed, as is removing all of them.

Limits and assumptions:
• 0 ≤ n ≤ 200000; 0 ≤ tokens[i] ≤ 10^6; 0 ≤ target ≤ 10^12.
• Sums fit in signed 64-bit integers. Return only the number of operations; keep the array unchanged.

Examples:
1. tokens = [1,1,4,2,3], target = 5 → 2, removing 2 and 3 from the right.
2. tokens = [0,0,5,0], target = 5 → 2, leaving the leading zeros.
3. tokens = [2,2], target = 3 → -1.

Choose one approach.
constraints: Sums fit in signed 64-bit integers. Return only the number of operations; keep the array unchanged.

options.text: Compute total-target. If negative return -1. Find the longest contiguous middle with that exact sum using a non-negative sum window, allowing the empty middle when the needed sum is zero. Return n minus its length, or -1 if no middle qualifies.
options.feedback: End removals leave one contiguous middle. Minimizing removed positions is equivalent to maximizing the kept length; zeros require preserving the longest exact-sum candidate.

options.text: Build prefix and suffix sum arrays. For each number removed from the left, binary-search the non-overlapping suffix choices for the fewest right removals achieving the target, and minimize their total.
options.feedback: Non-negative values make suffix sums non-decreasing, so a lower-bound search is valid, but the arrays and repeated searches can be replaced by one middle-window scan.

options.text: Repeatedly remove the larger available end until the removed total reaches or exceeds target.
options.feedback: For tokens [2,3,1] and target=4, this removes 2 and then 3, overshooting. Removing 1 and then 3 from the right reaches four in two operations.

options.text: Find the shortest contiguous middle with sum total-target and return n minus its length.
options.feedback: For [0,0,5,0], target=5 the needed sum is zero. Keeping two leading zeros needs two removals, while an empty middle would require four.

feedback.reason: Removing a prefix and suffix leaves one contiguous middle whose sum must equal total-target.
details: Set needed=sum(tokens)-target; return -1 if needed<0. For needed=0 initialize best=0 for the empty middle; otherwise best is absent. Extend a sum window and remove left values only while sum>needed. Whenever sum==needed record the greatest length. Return n-best if a candidate exists, otherwise -1.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only “Maximize the kept middle” as specified in the method reveal. Choose the tightest worst-case running-time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Use unit-cost random access and arithmetic on machine words large enough for every index and sum.
Input is read-only and excluded from auxiliary space. The scalar or index-pair output is excluded; no candidate segment is copied.
The implementation is iterative with a constant call stack. No hashing is used; fixed alphabet arrays, when present, are direct indexed.

options.text: O(n log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: One total scan and one nonnegative-sum window scan use fixed state.
details: Each legal choice of end removals leaves a contiguous middle, including empty. Non-negative sums support monotone repair; retaining zeros when equality holds finds the longest middle. Computing total and moving both boundaries take linear work and scalar storage.
“O(n²) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The longest retained middle is found with monotone boundaries, not by enumerating all removed prefix/suffix pairs.
“O(n log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: A total scan and nonnegative-sum window scan need no sorting, prefix table, or copied middle.
“O(n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: Only needed, sum, best length, and boundaries are retained; candidate middles are represented by indices.
